observedFacts: SUPPLIED: Controller Windows/PowerShell has no sbatch and no GPU; this says nothing about remote scheduler or allocated-node devices.
SUPPLIED: Authorized login host hpc-login uses Linux/Bash and provides Slurm, Apptainer and trusted module initialization.
SUPPLIED AUTHORIZATION: Only scoped read-only login-node discovery and script preparation are allowed. Actual submission/allocation and heavy solver tests are not authorized.
SUPPLIED: Inputs can be staged in shared storage /project/orders. Slurm does not itself stage those inputs.
SUPPLIED: Solver requires a GPU allocation and an explicit checkpoint argument. Remote tool/module versions, exact solver restart option and checkpoint semantics have not been established.
nextSteps: Controller: prepare LF-terminated Bash/batch drafts as files; validate paths and transfer/staging identity using the site's approved path. Preserve the site stack; do not install scheduler clients locally or replace MPI/CUDA/Apptainer.

Login: discover installed versions/help, current modules and narrowly relevant site/account/partition/resource guidance through the trusted initialization path. Capture module list stdout/stderr independently; normal module information may be on stderr.

Record resolved executables, versions, module identities and trusted initialization path. Never use automatic module purge, guessed source paths, an indiscriminate environment export, or execute unreviewed site/repository scripts.

Prepare batch draft rooted at /project/orders with explicit reviewed account/partition/GPU/CPU/memory/wall-time values, bounded output/checkpoint paths and pinned image/input identity. Keep unresolved values clearly marked; do not produce a falsely ready-to-submit script.

Restart draft contract: on initial run use the documented explicit checkpoint-output argument; on restart select only a compatible completely/atomically published checkpoint and use the documented explicit checkpoint/restart argument. Discover exact flags from trusted solver docs; do not invent --checkpoint syntax.

Slurm requeue starts the script again and signals do not create a checkpoint. Determine application format, atomic publication, frequency and signal handling; fit checkpoint I/O within preemption notice, preserve incomplete writes, and prevent duplicate committed results using durable run/output identity.

Separate Bash syntax from scheduler validation: bash -n is offline syntax only; sbatch --test-only contacts scheduler and validates neither runtime devices nor successful workload. Any scheduler contact must remain scoped and bounded; no submission occurs here.

Allocated-node steps are a future authorization gate: first verify assigned GPU and actual driver/toolkit/container/launcher/fabric compatibility, then a small representative authorized test, then checkpoint/restart and failure probes. Do not run solver/GPU work on login node.

Acceptance remains UNVERIFIED until an authorized allocation proves explicit checkpoint restore, useful computation and durable output completion, including interruptions before/after checkpoint/output commit. Record queue wait, useful GPU time, checkpoint time/bytes, lost work and restore time separately.
